chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the child who steals. He said: If he is seven years old or less, he is excused (handed over/not punished). If he returns (steals again) after seven, his fingers are cut or scraped until they bleed. If he returns, the part below his fingers is cut. If he returns after that and has reached nine years old, his hand is cut. And the limit of Allah is not neglected. It is possible that the two reports are carried upon one who knows the obligation of cutting upon him from the children in theft, even if he has not yet reached puberty, for if it is so, it is permissible for the Imam to cut his hand.
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a child who steals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Isfār establishes the specific age of criminal responsibility for theft in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the minor (sabi) and the mature (mumayyiz) through a graduated penal code. It highlights the Imam's discretionary authority (ta'zir) to apply hand amputation to children under puberty if they possess sufficient understanding, thereby linking the physical punishment to cognitive maturity rather than age alone. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that hudud limits are not rigidly fixed by age but are contingent upon the individual's capacity to comprehend the prohibition.
